hook: Sit in on a job interview and catch the facts that matter: the old job, the reasons, the hours and the final question.
intro: A job interview, heard once: Herr Brandt from a small company and Frau Wagner, who wants to change from selling furniture to an office job. It is the conversation you may one day have yourself, and the questions follow the interview in order: what she did before (Perfekt: hat … gearbeitet), why she wants the new job (a weil-clause), which language matters, how many hours the job has, why part-time suits her, and what she asks at the end (an indirect question: Könnten Sie mir sagen, wie …?). The Konjunktiv II is the sound of politeness on both sides — Ich würde gern …, Wäre das für Sie in Ordnung?, Könnten Sie mir sagen …? Listen for the numbers (drei Jahre, zwanzig Stunden, acht bis zwölf Uhr), the reasons after weil, and who is speaking.
tips[0].title: The interview script
tips[0].text: Erzählen Sie etwas über sich. · Ich habe … als … gearbeitet. · Ich würde gern …, weil … · Welche Sprachen sprechen Sie? · Haben Sie noch Fragen an uns? · Könnten Sie mir sagen, …? Each line opens a question slot.
tips[0].check.why: This line closes an interview and hands the floor over: now the applicant asks, often politely with Könnten Sie mir sagen, …?

tips[1].title: Reasons come after weil — and after deshalb
tips[1].text: weil sends the reason to the end of its clause: …, weil ich gut organisieren kann. deshalb gives the consequence with the verb second: …, deshalb ist Englisch für uns wichtiger. Two reason questions, two signal words.
tips[1].check.why: The reason is the clause after weil: meine Tochter ist noch klein.
tips[2].title: Numbers that sound alike
tips[2].text: The trap numbers sit close together: zwanzig Stunden (the week) and bis zwölf Uhr (the day). Note each number with the word next to it — Stunden or Uhr.
tips[2].check.why: The number next to Uhr is the clock time (zwölf); the number next to Stunden is the length (zwei).
remember[0]: Perfekt for what she did; würde gern for what she wants; weil for why.
remember[1]: Numbers and languages are always asked — catch them the first time.
exam: Two-person conversations like this job interview are a standard listening text in the B1 exam — and a real hurdle when you apply for work.
